title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page (situation (53)): X is a topological space and x ∈ X is a point at which X is a surface. D_x^* is the punctured germ at x, i.e. the pro-system of punctured discs D_{x,i}^* centred at x. Rev(D_x^*) is an ordinary Galois category. Its fundamental group is canonically the orientation module T_x of X at x (a rank-1 free Z-module, the topological analogue of Z(1)); this is (56). The universal coverings D_x^{*~} of the germ form a connected groupoid with automorphism group T_x. Grothendieck fixes one such D_x^{*~}.

On this page:
- He generalises from X−{x} to U = X∖S, where S is any subset in which x is an isolated point, for example a discrete set of punctures (57). The punctured germ then still embeds in U.
- He considers the composite D_x^{*~} → D_x^* ↪ U (58).
- If Rev(U) is multi-Galois (for instance U locally 1-connected), D_x^{*~} serves as a 'base point'. The fibre functor is Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~}) ≃ Sets, by pulling back a covering U' to D_x^{*~} and taking global sections. Its automorphism group is the fundamental group π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) (59).
- He announces a canonical homomorphism K_x : T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) (60). It is described as the map π_1(D_x^*, D_x^{*~}) ≅ T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) induced by the inclusion D_x^* ↪ U (61).
- The next page makes this concrete. T_x acts on D_x^{*~} by deck transformations, hence on Γ(D_x^{*~}, U' ×_U D_x^{*~}).
- He then compares this with a fundamental group π_1(U, Ũ) already chosen via a universal covering Ũ. That comparison needs a 'class of paths', i.e. an isomorphism between Ũ and the universal covering attached to the fibre functor at D_x^{*~}.

In modern terms: this is the topological prototype of tangential base points (base points at a puncture). It also constructs the canonical local-monodromy, or inertia, generator at a puncture, landing in π_1 with that base point. The purpose is to set up the discrete and profinite surface-group and Teichmüller-tower formalism of the Longue Marche / Esquisse. There, the loops around punctures, with their canonical orientation-module 'generators', are the basic data, e.g. for the 'cusp' or inertia structure of π_1 of a punctured surface.
errors: No mathematical error. The hypothesis 'U loc. 1-connexe' should be read as locally connected and locally (or semi-locally) simply connected, which suffices for Rev(U) to be multi-Galois.

Notational point only: D_x^* and D_x^{*~} are germs (pro-objects), so 'D_x^* ↪ U' means the punctured discs are eventually contained in U. This needs x isolated in S, which Grothendieck explicitly assumes.
The annotation under (60) writes the fibre functor as Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~}). This target is equivalent to Sets because D_x^{*~} is simply connected; that equivalence is implicit.

ideas.what: Using the universal covering of a punctured disc germ as a 'base point' for π_1 of U = X∖S, via the fibre functor Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~}) ≃ Sets
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point / base point at a puncture (topological version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Grothendieck's 'points base' at cusps in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and the Longue Marche (1981) discuss base points at cusps/tangential base points; this precise germ-of-universal-cover formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism K_x : T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) from the orientation module (local π_1 of the punctured germ) to the global fundamental group
ideas.modern_name: local monodromy / inertia (cusp) generator; peripheral subgroup of a punctured surface group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical topology (peripheral loops); algebraic analogue: tame inertia ≅ Ẑ'(1) in SGA1 XIII / Grothendieck–Murre
ideas.where_published: Algebraic analogue in SGA 1 Exp. XIII and Grothendieck–Murre (1971); topological version in the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Fundamental group defined as the automorphism group of a fibre functor of a multi-Galois category, with 'base points' given by any object whose covering category is trivial
ideas.modern_name: Galois category / fibre-functor formalism, groupoid of fibre functors

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard setup of base points at punctures (a topological version of tangential base points) and of the canonical inertia map from the orientation module. Grothendieck's own published Longue Marche / Esquisse framework already contains these ideas, and Deligne made them standard. Nothing on the page goes beyond the known record.
transcription_corrections: The word before (57) is 'pris' (continuing 'et soit … pris'). The label '(57)' is written below it.
Under 'Si', a crossed-out underlined 'Rev(…)' precedes the retained 'Rev(U)'. 'loc.' is inserted above '1-connexe'.
The annotation under (60) reads '≃ Aut du foncteur fibre Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~}) sur Rev(U)', consistent with the given transcription.
In (61), the isomorphism sign under π_1(D_x^*, D_x^{*~}) is a vertical '≀' ('21' in the scan), pointing to T_x.
